q: If you heat ice, it ___.
If it rains tomorrow, we ___ at home.
If I ___ rich, I would travel the world.
e: Second conditional: if + past ('were' for all persons).

q: If she had studied harder, she ___ the exam.
e: Third conditional: would have + past participle.

q: If I ___ you, I would accept the offer.
Unless governments ___ now, the problem will get worse.
e: 'Unless' = if not, so the verb is positive and present.

q: If I had taken that job, I ___ in London now.
e: Mixed conditional: past condition, present result.

q: If I ___ (have) more time, I would learn Italian.
If you ___ (not / hurry), you will miss the bus.
If we had left earlier, we ___ (not / miss) the flight.
e: Third conditional result: would (not) have + participle.

q: Plants die if they ___ (not / get) enough water.
e: Zero conditional: present in both parts.

q: What would you do if you ___ (win) the lottery?
If I see him, I ___ (tell) him the news.
If I will have time tomorrow, I'll call you.
fix: If I have time tomorrow, I'll call you.

q: If I would be rich, I'd buy a house by the sea.
fix: If I were rich, I'd buy a house by the sea.
e: No 'would' in the if-clause: use the past simple.

q: If she would have asked me, I'd have helped her.
fix: If she had asked me, I'd have helped her.

q: Unless you don't study, you will fail the exam.
fix: Unless you study, you will fail the exam.

q: I don't have a car, so I take the bus.
hint: Second conditional. Begin: If I had a car, ...
a: If I had a car, I would not take the bus.
If I had a car, I'd not take the bus.
e: Unreal present: if + past, would + verb.

q: She didn't study, so she failed.
hint: Third conditional. Begin: If she had studied, ...
a: If she had studied, she would not have failed.
If she had studied, she would have passed.
e: Unreal past: if + past perfect, would have + participle.

q: Take an umbrella or you will get wet.
a: If you don't take an umbrella, you will get wet.
